title: Nicholas Wotton to Queen Mary, June 1554 (BL Harley MS 1582 ff. 8-10; DECODE R8499)

plaintext.source: Contemporary deciphered copy at Harley MS 1582 ff. 5r-7v (BL catalogue); not digitised, not used.

transcription.notes: First transcription in ad-hoc tokens made before the key was found; several tokens merge distinct key signs.

system.summary: Graphic-sign letter substitution with 3-6 homophones per letter, about 16 nulls ('Nihil significantia') and a nomenclator of ~150 names and common words (and, the, of, to, was, the Constable, Peter Carew, the rebels, your highness ...). Nulls present.
system.notes: Key sheet on DECODE as R354 (TNA SP 106/2 f. 162, 'France 1554'); overbar/underline/dot variants distinguish codes.

prior_solution.where: Harley MS 1582 ff. 5r-7v, contemporary deciphered copy (not digitised)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up the coding agent with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R8499 record and 6 full-resolution images with the session cookie.
CSP Foreign Mary, June and July 1554 (BHO): only Wotton to Petre 14 June and to the Queen 14/29 July; this letter not calendared. Cryptiana has only Wotton's 1548 cipher.
Transcribed four cipher pages sign by sign in ad-hoc tokens (3,152 signs, 150 types) plus clear connectives; identified sender (Wotton) and recipient (the Queen) from the clear text.
Blind homophonic annealing (en-1640s): first solver collapsed (model artefact on 'eeee'); rewritten incremental annealer solved synthetic controls, but not R8499.
Synthetic English under 100/150-sign homophonic keys: 100% recovered clean; 1 run in 3 at 10% noise; fails at 20% noise.
DECODE R354 (SP 106/2 f. 162, France 1554): alphabet, nulls and nomenclator (Carew, the rebels, the Constable, Lady Elizabeth ...) of Wotton's 1554 cipher.

Nulls removed, key codes and letter values pinned, rest annealed: partial English (Compiegne, the rebels, the Constable, fair words, the pensions, the Low Countries, the resolution taken between the Constable and Carew).
Direct reading of p1.02 against the key: 'Compiegne and spake of ... with your highness the rebels with the Constable'.
Key-aligned readings of every line by 5 agents from the images, then 2 regrade passes with merged keys: p1-2 46.0% (744/1616), p3+p6 48.5% (644/1329) of signs read as sense.
Merged tokens re-checked on the images and split into precise labels (transcription_v2.txt); pinned anneal on v2 reads more sense, still well below 95%.
v3 regrade on the image-checked transcription: 2061/2737 non-null signs read (75.3%, incl. tentative); firm about 60%.
v4: unified key; 1765/2736 non-null signs read firmly (64.5%), 79.5% incl. tentative.
Full-resolution sign-by-sign passes on pages 1-2: p1 66% firm, p2 74% firm; whole letter 2016/2749 firm (73.3%).
Full-resolution sign-by-sign passes on pages 3 and 6; whole letter 1971/2750 firm (71.7%), 88.3% incl. tentative.
Unified key v6 and full transcription of the R354 nomenclator (~140 entries); whole letter 2092/2797 firm (74.8%), 89.2% incl. tentative.
Full nomenclator tested against every unread stretch: few codes fit; whole letter 75.0% firm, 89.5% incl. tentative (v7).

Full-resolution shape pass: ^ and C each split into two shapes matching their context values; rare codes absent from R354; name lookup proposes 'Brymstane, a Scot'. 75.0% firm, 89.4% incl. tentative (v8).

Harleian catalogue 1808 and BL catalogue: ff. 5r-7v is a contemporary copy deciphering ff. 8-10 (13 June 1554, Soissons); not digitised and not on DECODE. Tytler ii, CSP Scotland i and DECODE key search found nothing further.

Isle of Wight sentence (f. 8r p1.13-16) re-read on the image against the R354 key: 'concludid' confirmed; the Ie sign given as 'also' (I); the 13 signs after 'taken' tried with every key alternative and an en-1640s brute force ('...privates' best, not adopted) and left unread.
Sense measure written (measure_sense.py, sense_judgement.tsv): the old measure counted letter-for-letter readings without sense; v8 is 74.3% by the old measure but 68.4% read as sense.

Full-resolution image re-transcription of unread stretches: p2.25 name read as 'Brimstane, a Scot' (13 of 15 signs); p1.24 '(fy)ve hundrid' tentative; p1.13 run confirmed on the image and still unread after an LM brute force; Stafford 1586 key (harley1582r8500) found to be a different system. Sense 68.9% (final_v9.txt).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2876 tokens, 212 types, en-1640s order 4: reading -2.332 per letter; random keys -3.575 (z 10.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.529 (mean -2.543, z 12.9); annealer on the real text -2.385. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the v4 page transcriptions and final_v9.txt (latest tokens per line with the reading); key = R354 as read plus the unified key v6, the v7 codes, the shape pass and the nomenclator

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): final_v9.txt read through; holes and broken grammar in most sentences (10% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py), only the gist and phrases build. The one document relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read after matching with key from external sources -> not solved; fraction_read 0.689 -> 0.

Re-read brief b28, step 1: every DECODE record of Harley MS 1582 listed from the DECODE harvest and re-fetched with the cookie (b28_fetch.py): R8499 has no attachment or comment; R8009 is an empty record; R8010's four images are ff. 263r-264v (the Navarre memoir, same leaves as R8505), not the Wotton decipherment ff. 5r-7v. BL catalogue (23 Oct 2026) now lists Harley 1582 as digitised but its images unavailable (ark:/81055/vdc_100162940894.0x000001); IIIF manifest routes return 403/404.

Reading judged again (final_v9.txt): 0.102 clean sentences (10/98), hole rate 0.317; no new image pass (v9 already re-read every line at full resolution); stays decoded, not read, blocker needs-physical-access (ff. 5r-7v).

Method restored: key obtained by matching the key DECODE R354 (SP 106/2 f. 162), filed in another series (read after matching with key from external sources); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Read share over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), checked: the NOTES' 'whole letter' figures are over the non-null cipher signs of all four pages, not clear and cipher together; R8499 is decoded, not read, and carries no read_share. No figure or class changed.

outcome.method_basis: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: the key DECODE R354 (TNA SP 106/2 f. 162, 'France 1554'), filed in another series, was matched to R8499 and applied and corrected over eight passes, but the decode does not build sentences (holes in most of them), so no reading is claimed. The contemporary clear copy (Harley 1582 art. 2, ff. 5r-7v) is not digitised. Before: read after matching with key from external sources. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by matching the key DECODE R354 (SP 106/2 f. 162), filed in another series; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: the one document is decoded, not read, so no tokens are counted as read. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.689 = share of non-null signs judged sense, unread or tentative excluded (measure_sense.py, 5 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R8499, Nicholas Wotton to Queen Mary, Soissons, 13 June 1554 (Harley MS 1582 ff. 8-10)
texts.summary: Dr Nicholas Wotton, English ambassador in France, reports to Queen Mary that Peter Carew was at Compiègne and spoke with the French king and the Constable, on the English rebels in France, and that the Constable discussed with Carew how the Isle of Wight might be taken and kept. Read with the 1554 France key DECODE R354; about 31% of non-null signs remain unread or tentative, and the contemporary decipherment (ff. 5r-7v) is not digitised. final_v9.txt gives the tokens per line beside the reading.
